title: Wavelet coalescence lab diary - selene
content:
Context and goal:
This is a personal scratchpad for the 'wavelet coalescence' experiment: create a controlled superposition of short, overlapping request pulses (wavelets) to observe how the runtime's batching/coalescing heuristics and KV-cache interactions affect tail latency and GPU utilization. Aim: understand when coalescing helps vs when it amplifies p99 under multi-tenant noise.

Test rig and data:
- Cluster: 4x A100 (80GB) in a single pod, serving the same 7B model variant (int8 quantized).
- Runtime build: local branch wavelet-coalesce-experiments (PR linked above).
- Traffic generator: modified k6 + custom python driver to schedule wavelets (see wavelet-scheduler.py).
- Workload: short-conversation payloads (~40 tokens request, ~160 tokens response). Mix 80% Gen, 20% Rerank small.
- Key metrics captured: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (server-side), tail tokens/sec, batching size distribution, KV cache hit rate, GPU SM utilization, per-request cost estimate.

Wavelet pattern definition:
- Base inter-arrival: Poisson lambda tuned to 120 qps steady.
- Wavelet: 200ms duration pulses with triangular envelope, amplitude +300 qps above base, spacing random uniform 1.2s-3.0s.
- Superposition: allow up to 3 simultaneous wavelets to overlap (phase offsets).

Run notes (iterative):
1) 2026-02-16 10:12 - dry run (no cache warmup)
   - Observations: huge p99 spikes during first 30s of wavelet onset (~2.6s), batching lag grew to 250ms.
   - Hypothesis: cold KV cache + initial batching ramp creates empty-slot waits.

2) 2026-02-18 14:05 - warmed cache (cache primed with synthetic prefix), default coalescing settings
   - p50: 48ms, p95: 220ms, p99: 890ms (worst peaks ~1.1s).
   - Batch size mean: 6, distribution: {1:22%, 2-5:58%, 6-12:18%, >12:2%} (quick counts from logs).
   - KV cache hit: 67% overall; during wavelet overlap it dips to ~52% (more unique contexts simultaneously).
   - GPU util: spiky, avg 63%, peaks to 95% during overlapping wavelets.

3) 2026-02-22 09:30 - increased coalesce_timeout (default +50ms) and enabled early-flush threshold for latency-sensitive lanes
   - Result: median unchanged, p95 improved (~190ms), p99 reduced to ~610ms.
   - Tradeoff: throughput decreased ~4% during steady periods; slightly higher small-batch frequency.

4) 2026-02-28 16:40 - enabled conservative-prefill (limit speculative prefetches) + tuned batching window adaptive (shorter for high-variance lanes)
   - p50: 46ms, p95: 170ms, p99: 420ms.
   - KV hit stabilized ~70%.
   - Observed that conservative-prefill reduced sudden GPU memory pressure (less swapping for kv cache).

Quick visual notes (referenced charts saved in /tmp):
- wavelet_qps_p99_overlay.png -> overlay of QPS waveform and p99 spikes, shows correlation when two wavelets overlap.
- batch_hist_wavelet.png -> bimodal batch-size distribution during experiments with overlapping wavelets.

Preliminary conclusions:
- Coalescing heuristics need to be phase-aware: when multiple short wavelets overlap, naive coalescing increases waiting time for early arrivals, amplifying p99.
- KV cache contention / memory pressure is a second-order amplifier: when many unique contexts land simultaneously, cache thrashing causes decoding stalls and latency spikes.
- Shortening coalesce_timeout plus early-flush under high-variance lanes reduces p99 but costs a few percent steady throughput. Still likely a net win for customer-facing low-latency workloads.
- Conservative prefill (reduce speculative allocations) helps with memory pressure without much impact on p50.

Action items / TODOs:
- [ ] Run the same suite but with a 13B distill variant to see model-size sensitivity (ticketed INF-7321).
- [ ] Add per-request backpressure tagging to trace pipeline, so we can see which requests were delayed due to coalescing vs cache miss.
- [ ] Explore a 'phase detector' in the ingress that flags overlapping wavelets (use FFT short-window) and temporarily adjusts coalesce rules. Quick prototype idea: 250ms sliding window energy metric -> if energy > X, set lane to low-latency mode.
- [ ] Write a short runbook describing how to pick coalesce_timeout based on observed ingress frequency spectrum.

Open questions / weirdness to investigate:
- Why does KV hit rate dip more than expected given cache size? Possible allocation fragmentation in HBM (open with infra: github PR linked).
- There are occasional 2x p99 spikes with no corresponding QPS blip; need to correlate with node-level background GC/driver resets. Add smoothed telemetry overlays.

Notes to self:
- Keep this file as the running lab diary; when we stabilize, move a polished summary to Confluence and link from INF-7321.
- If I get a consistent recipe for coalesce_timeout + early-flush heuristics, propose a default low-latency profile in the console.

Experiment artifact pointers (local):
- /tmp/wavelet_runs/run_2026_02_28/metrics.csv
- /tmp/wavelet_runs/run_2026_02_28/batch_hist.json
- /tmp/wavelet_runs/run_2026_02_22/trace_sample_42.json

End of scratchpad for now. Notes will be appended after next runs.
